goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Turn, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for: the person, a work they put to use as it is handed over, having decided only what is theirs; the calling AI, a work made for its person on the points it settled, which it passes on as it is.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:21 "They get a work that meets their purpose well, and spend effort only where only they can decide."

questions.what: Reading an objective, does the developer know which user the product is for and what that user gets from it?
Weighing a piece of work, can the developer tell which one objective it brings closer?
After a change, can the developer tell from the key results whether users came closer to the objective?
Weighing a change that shortens the lead time, can the developer tell whether it keeps how well the user gets what the objective says?
For each objective, can the developer follow, step by step, how its user goes from when they first need it to having what the objective says?
Building a step of a scenario, can the developer tell whether it waits for a person, is taken by an AI, or runs as a script?
Can the developer change how the product works inside, while its users see the same, and leave the document as it is?

decisions.what: Who comes to Turn with a goal of their own?
decisions.decided: Two users. The person: the one who wants a work made, such as a README or a module of code, and will put it to use. The calling AI: an AI that connects a person and Turn, such as a role of another plugin that carries a larger plan for the person, and has Turn make a work the plan needs. It comes with a goal of its own: it hands over what it already settled with its person and wants that kept, and it must pass the work on. Turn's own roles, the AI that a design from Pin is handed to inside Turn, and the plugins Turn depends on come with no goal of their own, so none is a user. Differs from the old UX, which named the caller by a plugin, rn, and made it a user of an objective about handing over alone.

decisions.what: Which plugins may the document name, and what work do the examples use?
decisions.decided: Turn only. The calling AI is named by its role, never by a plugin that calls Turn. Lane and Pin, which Turn depends on, run inside Turn, so by D13 the document leaves them out too. Both scenarios make a README for `tidy`, a command-line tool that sorts a Downloads folder, the same work as the README's walkthrough, so the developer meets one example across both documents. A README is a kind Turn knows, as most requests will be.
grounds: ux.json Q7 thinking: "the document says only what users mean to do, see and receive, so any design that gives them the same leaves it true." A plugin that calls Turn can change or go while Turn's users see the same.
plugins/turn/README.md:74 "Your tool `tidy` sorts a Downloads folder into folders by type."

decisions.what: Which words does the document define before the objectives, so the objectives read on first sight?
decisions.decided: Four, each where first used, in the opening: a work, what the person wants made; its kind, the sort of work, such as a README; a point, one thing the work's design must settle, a fact or a decision; and the questions of a kind, those a good work of the kind answers yes to, which the person approves for a kind new to Turn. The design is not named on its own: "every point settled" says it. The person meets each of these words in what Turn shows them, so none is inside the box.
grounds: refactor-doc.json Q7 thinking: "gives its meaning where the reader first meets it."
plugins/turn/README.md:19 "For a kind it does not know, Turn first researches how good works of"
dev/pin/ux.md:11 "A point of a plan is one thing the plan must settle: a fact, such as what reads a file today, or a decision"

decisions.what: How many objectives, and cut by what?
decisions.decided: Two, one for each user and gain. O1, the person's: a work they put to use as it is, having decided only what is theirs, whether they ask Turn or a calling AI asks for them, and of any kind, known to Turn or new. O2, the calling AI's: its settled points kept and the work passed on as it is. The old O2, a work of a kind new to Turn, merges into O1: the gain is the same work for the same person, and the kind being new is only the case it comes in, so a piece of work on how Turn learns a new kind brings O1 closer through KR1.1 and KR1.2. Checked by ux.json Q2 step 2 on changes made or planned: the work judged by an AI that did not make it, a fix traced to the decision behind it, the reading bettered once every question is met, a template kept for later runs of a new kind, a stopped run going on from its folder, and parts made at once each bring O1 closer; the calling AI's settled points kept as given, a question for the person passed through it word for word, and the work kept where it named each bring O2 closer; the refactoring phase run by the same two roles instead of two of its own brings neither, as no user sees it, and so is a change for the architecture alone. Differs from the old UX, which had three objectives and gave the new kind one of its own.
grounds: ux.json Q2 step 1: "Merge objectives that one piece of work would bring closer together. Split an objective that holds gains a piece of work could bring closer apart."
ux.json Q2 step 2: "Take each change planned or recently made that alters what a user gets, and name the one objective it brings closer."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:85 "Turn has two making roles, generator and evaluator: the refactoring phase runs them with the refactoring template, the phase a run value"

decisions.what: O1, as one line with the user as its subject and no mechanism
decisions.decided: O1: The person gets a work they put to use as it is handed over, having decided only what is theirs. Checked by ux.json Q1 step 3: the old O1, a work that meets their purpose well, could be claimed by Turn's own checks while the person still mends the work; "put to use as it is handed over" holds the gain as the person meets it. "Having decided only what is theirs" holds the other half: they find no fact and settle no point Turn could have settled.

decisions.what: O2, as one line with the user as its subject and no mechanism
decisions.decided: O2: The calling AI has a work made for its person on the points it settled, and passes it on as it is. Checked by ux.json Q1 step 3: the old O3, handing Turn what it settled and getting a work back, could be done while the calling AI still rewords Turn's questions or mends the work; "on the points it settled" and "passes it on as it is" hold the gain. Whether the work then serves the person is O1's, so the gain is not counted twice.

ux.json Q1 step 3, as for D5.

decisions.what: How do success and failure of each objective show in what the user does?
decisions.decided: O1 fails where the person changes the work, or sends it back for a change, before they first put it to use; where the person is asked a point that is not theirs, such as a fact Turn could find or a decision that follows from the purpose, so they leave it to Turn or tell Turn the fact; where the person works around Turn, settling a point outside the run or having the work made another way; where the person gives up, stopping the run or setting the work aside; and, for a kind new to Turn, where the person changes a question of the kind after approving it. O2 fails where Turn asks the person a point the calling AI settled, or the work holds such a point otherwise; where the calling AI cannot pass a question on as given, so it rewords or answers it; where the calling AI works around Turn, changing the work or settling a point with the person itself before passing the work on; and where the calling AI gets no work back, as the run stops.
grounds: ux.json Q3 step 1: "For the objective, list how success or failure would show in what the user does or feels, such as giving up, undoing a result or working around the product."
ux.json Q3 grounds, Rodden et al.: "Sometimes failure is easier to identify than success"

decisions.what: What does each key result count?
decisions.decided: For each objective, a share of the works that go wrong, counted out of the works the user has Turn make, with D7's ways listed under it; then a lead time to the work the user keeps. Lower and shorter are better. A work counts once however many ways it goes wrong, so the share stays a share. Checked by ux.json Q3 step 3: KR1.1 cannot fall by asking the person everything, as a point not theirs counts, nor by asking nothing, as a point settled against their mind shows as a change; it cannot fall by delivering at once, as a work given up or sent back counts. KR1.2 runs to the work the person puts to use, so rounds of change count in it, and a fast first draft does not shorten it. KR2.1 counts the calling AI working around Turn, so it cannot fall while the calling AI still mends the work or settles points itself.
grounds: ux.json Q3 step 2: "Make each a share, an average per user, a count or a time, and name what it is counted out of."
ux.json Q3 step 3: "Ask whether all the objective's key results could get better while the user still does not get what the objective says. If so, add or rework key results until they could not."

decisions.decided: KR1.1: of the works the person has Turn make, directly or through a calling AI, the share that goes wrong, in D7's five ways for O1. KR1.2: the lead time from the person's request to the work they put to use, their answers and any rounds of change included. Differs from the old KR1.1, which mixed works and questions in one count and did not count giving up or working around Turn, and from the old KR1.2, which ended at the work handed back.
grounds: D7
D8

decisions.decided: KR2.1: of the works the calling AI has Turn make, the share that goes wrong, in D7's four ways for O2. KR2.2: the lead time from the calling AI's request to the work it gets back, the person's answers included. Differs from the old KR3.1, which counted the person's changes, now O1's, and not the calling AI rewording a question or working around Turn.

decisions.what: How does the developer weigh a change that shortens the lead time?
decisions.decided: Said once under the OKRs: in each objective the first key result comes first, and a change shortens the lead time only if it keeps the first as good. One example follows, phrased as a change being weighed, not as what Turn does: asking the person fewer points shortens KR1.2, and is kept only where no point the person would decide otherwise is then settled without them. Key results have no target values (Goodhart's law).
grounds: ux.json Q4 thinking: "Quality first, then lead time: each stage from the user's need to the result, such as asking, deciding, making and redoing, gets shorter only where the result stays as good"
ux.json Q4 steps: "Imagine the change, and ask whether it could make the first key result worse." "Keep it only where it could not."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:151 "The aim is to shorten the lead time without lowering quality."

decisions.what: Who takes part, and of what kind?
decisions.decided: The person (person), the calling AI (AI) and Turn (AI), one box for all Turn does, as Claude runs it. Each step the person takes waits for them. No step at this level runs as a script. What runs inside Turn, such as its roles and its checks, is no participant. Differs from the old UX, which listed the main conversation, up, planner, designer, generator, evaluator, refactorer and proofreader, a researcher, Lane, the checks and rn.
grounds: ux.json Q6 step 1: "In each scenario, name each participant it uses, with its kind, as the list of participants gives them"
ux.json Q7 grounds, Cockburn: "For computer systems, it is rare that we open up the black box."

decisions.what: What does the document show, and what does it leave to the README and the architecture?
decisions.decided: Only what the person and the calling AI do, see and receive: the request, the purpose to confirm, for a new kind the kind's purpose and questions to approve, one point at a time to confirm or decide, the design to approve, and the work handed back with each question shown met. Turn's roles, the order Lane starts them in, Pin, the run's files, the relay through the main conversation, the background runs and the parts made at once are inside the box. Checked by ux.json Q7 step 1 on one change, the refactoring phase run by generator and evaluator with the refactoring questions instead of by refactorer and proofreader: in the old UX the participant line of refactorer and proofreader and three arrows naming them were flagged; the new document names no role, and no line is flagged. Checked again on a second change, Turn settling the design without Pin and running its roles in the conversation instead of in the background: the old line "Every role runs in the background" was flagged and goes; no line of the new document is flagged.
grounds: ux.json Q7 step 1: "Pick one change the design could make while users see the same, read every line, and flag each line that would have to change."
ux.json Q7 step 2: "Rewrite each flagged line by what the user does, sees or receives, or leave it to the document that describes the design inside"

decisions.what: How much does a step of a scenario say?
decisions.decided: Each arrow says in a few words what one does to another. What is passed, such as a question's wording or the form of the run's files, is the spec, left to the README and the architecture. Differs from the old UX, whose arrows named roles, routes and checks.
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 2: "Write each step as one message, from the one who takes it to the one it acts on, saying what it passes, checks or changes"

decisions.decided: By its objective's ID and a short active phrase, the user its subject: "O1: The person has tidy's README made, deciding only what is theirs", "O2: The calling AI has tidy's README made on the points it settled".
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 1: "Name each scenario by its objective's ID and a short active verb phrase, the user its subject, saying how they reach it."

decisions.what: Where does each objective's gain show in its run?
decisions.decided: In two loops. The first runs until no point is open: Turn settles itself each point that follows from the purpose and the facts, and puts to the person one point alone, a fact it found to confirm or a decision of theirs with a recommendation. The second runs until the work meets every question of its kind and of how it reads: Turn makes the work and makes it again, asking the person nothing, except a point that comes up and is theirs, shown as an opt inside it. A kind new to Turn is an opt before the purpose: the person approves the kind's purpose and questions. In O2 the first loop runs through the calling AI, and Turn keeps what the calling AI settled without asking it again. Without the loops, the scenario would read the same as a work asked of Claude alone, and the reader could not see what the user gains.
grounds: ux.json Q5 step 3: "Mark a part that repeats as a loop with its condition, holding each step that repeats."
ux.json Q5 step 4: "each step moves toward it."

decisions.decided: The person types /turn:up with the work in their own words. For a kind new to Turn, the opt of D16. Turn puts the work's purpose to confirm, and the person says yes. The kind is not asked where the request names it, as that would ask a point that is not theirs. The first loop of D16 runs. Turn shows the design, each point in a short line, and the person approves it. The second loop runs. Turn hands the person the work, with each question shown met, written but not committed. Differs from the old UX in that no role, route or check appears.
